name: fill_makes_fourteen_holes
why: THE FILL PATTERN HAD NEVER BEEN BORN (GP14, W1.1): fifteen NULL combinations on FeatureFillPattern, which the API guide calls Obsolete, and seven NULLs on the new route written without a selection. The recipe of IFillPatternFeatureData (Remarks) and of Create_Fill_Pattern_Example_CSharp.htm is to preselect the feature (mark 4), the direction edge (mark 1) and the boundary face (mark 16384), then CreateDefinition with scalars only. The probe of 28/9/2026 (Checks/Fill/Program.cs, attempt A) measured it on THIS plate: on the top plane, 100 in X, 60 in Z, 12 in Y, the Ø8 through hole at X = -30, Z = 0, and as direction an edge along X of the top face (the boundary face). 14 more holes, volume 71396.8 -> 62952.2. The plate stays on the top plane, and not on the front one like the other cases of the folder, because the 14 is a number from the SOLIDWORKS algorithm and is compared only on the measured geometry; the edge is the one at z = +30 of the top face, which by symmetry (the plate and the hole are mirrored from z = 0) gives the same layout as the one at z = -30. The scalars of the example (pitch 17.0240490494193, 10 copies per loop, margin 0) are written equal to the probe.
_why_the_numbers: 72000 = 100 x 60 x 12. A Ø8 through hole over 12 removes pi x 4^2 x 12 = 603.186 mm3. After the fill the holes are 15 (the original plus the 14 copies measured by the probe): 72000 - 15 x 603.186 = 62952.21, and the change in volume is -14 x 603.186 = -8444.60. FOURTEEN CANNOT BE COMPUTED BY HAND, and we do not pretend to: how many copies fit is decided by the loop algorithm of SOLIDWORKS (the seed goes to the centre of the face, the guide says so, but it does not say the starting angle of the loops). What is computed by hand is that EVERY copy is a whole hole of 603.186 -- none bitten by the edge, none merged with another -- and the fifteen diameters of 8 say so with the position, not with the volume alone.

expect.why: THE PROBE'S PLATE: the top is XZ and the plate grows along +Y from y = 0, so the top face is at y = 12 and the direction edge of step 3 is written counting on this. If this is red, the fill is not to blame.

expect.tolerance_why: the diameter is read from CylinderParams, which returns metres
as above: the cylinder axis in metres
72000 minus pi*4^2*12: the calculation has pi inside
72000 minus 15 times pi*4^2*12: the calculation has pi inside
14 times pi*4^2*12, the -8444.6 measured by the probe
fifteen holes of 8: the diameter is read from CylinderParams
